title: Session Slicing, Redispatch, and Expert Oversubscription — Playbook + Notes
content:
Top-line summary:
This is a working playbook describing investigation and mitigations for a recurring long-tail latency mode we started seeing on MoE-backed Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants when processing multi-kiloton long-context sessions (>16k tokens). Key hypothesis: session window slicing + prefix KV staleness combine with expert oversubscription to trigger frequent redispatches and cross-GPU synchronization spikes.

Context and why this matters:
- Prod symptom: P95/P99 token latency spikes (2–8x) under steady load from a few heavy sessions. Not full cluster overload — only sessions with long rolling prefixes and high branching (many short user turns) reproduce.
- Customer impact: interactive experiences (code assistants, chat histories) see stutter; throughput targets missed for Dedicated customers on reservation-bound nodes.

Observed behavior (raw):
- Redispatch events correlate with KV cache mismatch across replicas. Traces show repeated fallthrough to full-key recompute at steps where prefix windows slide and tokenized chunk boundaries change.
- Expert fanout curves show temporary peaks where a small set of experts receives >3x expected tokens for a shard, causing hotspot queuing and kernel serialization.
- GPU cross-device memcpy and NCCL alltoall times increase sharply at the same time windows as kernel fusion failure logs.

Quick repro notes:
- Repro harness: reproduces with synthetic trace generator (long_session_fuzz.py) using 20 sessions of length 24k tokens with interleaved short responses. Use model variant: llama-70b-moe-2x, batch window target 32ms.
- Flags: --kv-slice=4096 --redispatch-threshold=0.3 --expert-cap=1.2

Metric signals to watch (recommended dashboards):
- per-session token completion latency (p50/p95/p99)
- per-expert instantaneous fanout and queued-ms
- kv-cache-hit-rate by session and partition
- redispatch-counts per route and per-host
- NCCL/alltoall p50/p95 and GPU memcpy counters

Experiment matrix we ran (short form):
- A. Increase KV slice to 8192 -> reduced redispatch frequency by ~22% but increased per-dispatch memory working set leading to higher GC-like eviction events.
- B. Cap expert fanout at 1.0 (soft limit) -> lowered P99 by ~18% but increased rejection rate for peak tokens (observed 0.6% of requests getting fallback to smaller model).
- C. Introduce small randomized token-aligned windowing (jitter window +/- 128 tokens) -> smoothed redispatch clustering, reduced alltoall spikes ~12%.
- D. Aggressive prefetch for next-window KV -> reduced redispatches in synthetic runs but observed new contention in UVM page faults on heterogeneous GPU hosts.

Deep-dive traces (notes):
- Trace A (2026-01-23 03:14UTC): session id s-7f2b, token idx 17812 -> redispatch triggered after sliding window boundary crosses subtoken boundary. Router logs: gating entropy low, expert set unchanged, but kv-checksum mismatch flagged. Kernel timeline: tokenization->router->prefetch fails->redispatch->fallback gather. Wall-time between initial router decision and final kernel execution: 14.8ms (median 4.1ms).
- Trace B (2026-02-05 16:02UTC): high expert fanout on expert-13: queued-ms increased from 0.9ms to 6.3ms across 7 consecutive mini-batches; NCCL alltoall p95 increased 4x. Postmortem: hot session had repeated short-turn updates causing repeated reassignments.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV staleness detection is too conservative — triggers redispatch on benign tokenization shifts rather than true cache-invalidating edits.
2) Session-slicing heuristic aligns poorly with subtoken boundaries in multilingual/text-with-emoji workloads causing frequent small shifts.
3) Expert oversubscription is amplified by small-window batching that reduces statistical smoothing of expert assignments.
4) Heterogeneous host memory (UVM) plus aggressive prefetch creates page fault cascades when slices overlap heavily.

Short-term mitigations (can be shipped as runtime flags):
- opt:kv_strictness=low -> relax checksum sensitivity for sliding-window mismatches (safe for read-only inference; caveat: risks rare stale prefix effects).
- introduce: session-window-jitter=128 -> low-cost randomized offset to break synchronized boundary events across sessions.
- soft-expert-cap=1.05 with local queuing -> prevent single-expert bursts from serializing kernels and force slight rejection/fallback early.
- redispatch-backoff policy: exponential backoff per-session to avoid repeated immediate redispatch storms.

Longer term work / proposals:
- Adaptive KV validity: attach lightweight vector summary per slice (bloom or fingerprint) and use probabilistic checks to avoid full redispatch when mismatch is low probability.
- Router-aware slicing: make slicing algorithm router-informed so windows align with typical gating boundaries (learn from historical gating masks).
- Per-expert admission controller that tracks moving-window fanout and throttles token admission upstream rather than at serialized kernel time.
- Re-evaluate UVM prefetch heuristics on heterogeneous fleets — add host-type selective prefetch policy.

Operational playbook (for oncall):
1) Detect: alert on redispatch-rate > 0.5% of tokens over 5m or per-host alltoall p95 > baseline*3.
2) Short-term rollback: toggle opt:kv_strictness=low and session-window-jitter=128 on affected pool.
3) Mitigate hotspots: apply soft-expert-cap on routing group; if still hot, route affected sessions to smaller model variant (policy-based fallback).
4) Post-incident: capture representative traces, export NVTX and NCCL timelines, and save to /var/run/si-traces/<incident-id>. Reference: JIRA-RT-1438.

Open questions / investigation threads:
- How often do real-world prompts (multi-lingual + emoji + code + pasted long docs) actually shift subtoken boundaries compared to our synthetic split? Need corpus analysis (task: Priya to run ngram/subtoken-shift audit on customer corpus).
- What is the safe window for kv_strictness relaxation without causing observable historical regression in output coherence? A/B test candidate.
- Can we leverage cached gating masks (persisted lightweight) to reduce repeated computation across sliding windows?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add sample trace extractor script and link to PR (Diego TODO).
- Run longitudinal test across heterogeneous hosts (8xA100, 4xH100 mixed) to see UVM prefetch interactions (Liam TODO).
- Draft a short customer-facing explanation for Dedicated customers explaining the tradeoffs of relaxed kv_strictness (marketing/legal signoff required).

Relevant quick links:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2976 (redispatch backoff prototype)
- JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RT-1438
- Confluence draft: confluence://serving/runtime/redispatch-playbook

Appendix: quick checklist for experiments to reproduce locally
- start local harness with: python long_session_fuzz.py --model llama-70b-moe-2x --hosts 4 --kv-slice 4096 --session-count 20 --seed 42
- enable tracing: export SI_NVTX=1 && SI_NCCL_TRACE=1
- collect traces: scripts/collect_traces.sh <output-dir>

End of playbook (WIP).

omments: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and incomplete — it's meant as a working lab notebook for the eng-serving-runtime team. Expect follow-ups and a more formal postmortem if/when we see a customer-facing incident.
